new_task_1.title: Clarify duplicate parametrization errors for repeated argument names
new_task_1.description: When parametrization attempts to define the same argument more than once, pytest still raises a ValueError, but the message is now explicit that the failure is caused by duplicate parametrization of that argument instead of the vaguer previous wording.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that duplicate parametrization failures report a clear, specific error message identifying the problem as repeated parametrization of the same argument name.

expectation.grounded: When `CallSpec2` detects that an argument name already exists in `params` or `funcargs` while processing a new parametrization entry, it must raise `ValueError` with the message `duplicate parametrization of {arg!r}`.
expectation.conceptual: If a test or fixture parametrizes the same argument twice, pytest should fail with an error message that clearly explains the cause so users can diagnose conflicting parametrization declarations quickly.

constraints.grounded: The duplicate detection condition remains unchanged: the exception is raised when the argument is already present in either `params` or `funcargs`. Only the wording of the raised `ValueError` changes.
constraints.conceptual: The change should improve diagnostic clarity without altering when pytest rejects duplicate parametrization.

behavior: Pytest continues to reject duplicate parametrization of the same argument name.
The exception message now explicitly says `duplicate parametrization of 'argname'` instead of the less specific `duplicate 'argname'` wording.
acceptance_criteria: Given a test setup that parametrizes the same argument name more than once, when pytest builds the call specification, then it raises `ValueError`.
Given that duplicate-parametrization failure, when the error message is rendered, then it contains the phrase `duplicate parametrization of` followed by the duplicated argument name.
Given valid parametrization with unique argument names, when pytest builds the call specification, then no new error is introduced by this change.
